name: Rufus
look: an old Roman fisherman with a white beard, an olive felt cap, a cream shirt and olive brown work clothes, a mended net over his shoulder
lines: Bream like a shrimp on the hook, and they bite best in the morning.
Rain brings the fish up. Don't stay home when it rains.

name: Prima
look: a sturdy Roman fishwife in a brown tunic carrying a basket of fish
lines: Sell a bit of everything. Nobody wants ten mullet at once.
The market forgets by morning. Prices climb back overnight.

name: Tertius
look: a barefoot Roman boy of ten with tousled brown hair in a short pale tunic with a red belt, grinning
lines: I'd pull your pots for you if you paid me!
Old Rufus says morays only come out for squid.

name: Aulus
look: a thin Roman salt seller in a pale tunic with a sack of salt
lines: Salt your catch and it keeps. Not as dear, but it keeps.
Garum needs salt by the measure, and patience by the week.

name: Secunda
look: a young Roman woman baker in a flour-dusted apron holding round loaves
lines: The mullet in the harbour come for my crusts.
Sardines nibble bread near the surface. Easy to net, they say.

name: Marcus
look: a tanned Roman sailor in a red tunic with a coil of rope
lines: Off Misenum the water goes down forever. You'll need a long line.
The swordfish run when the storms come through.

name: Faustina
look: a Roman girl flower seller with a basket of roses and myrtle
lines: My grandmother saw a golden bream in the Lucrine. She swore it ate oysters.
Ladies at Baiae put earrings on their morays. Truly!

name: Gaius
look: a Roman potter with clay on his hands carrying an amphora
lines: Every amphora of garum I make goes to Umbricius.
The ship to Rome sails every seventh day.

name: Livia
look: a smiling Roman innkeeper woman with a jug of wine
lines: The tuna come in spring. The whole town nets the bay together.
At night the squid come to a lamp like moths.

name: Decimus
look: a weathered old Roman sponge diver with a grey beard and tanned skin in a short faded blue tunic, a net bag of sponges over his shoulder
lines: There's a wreck off the rocky shore. Something huge lives in it.
The blue caves of Capri hide parrotfish.
